graphtheory.name: Graph Theory: What Connections Permit
graphtheory.truth: The same connections can host different journeys. What the graph leaves out will not be recovered by choosing another route.
graphtheory.qfep_connection: Ada uses graph encounters to ask what a representation makes reachable, cheap or permissible. These are distinct questions; a minimum, a drawing and an available route do not establish one universal measure of value.
graphtheory.description: Eight encounters distinguish visit order, drawing, route availability, network measures, directed return, minimum connection cost, capacity and pairing. Keep the relations visible as the question changes.
learning_objectives: Compare queue and stack traversals on one graph
Observe rerouting when a represented option disappears or returns
Distinguish drawn prominence from a measured relation
Trace directed paths and return paths
Distinguish minimum total connection cost from short journeys and resilience
Read capacity, preflow and excess; identify the missing reverse adjustments
Compare maximal and maximum matching through different edge orders on one graph
